subject: dec-concurrency-backend-framework
text: - **[Concurrency / Backend Framework] Hybrid sync core + Tokio only in `mcp` (KEYSTONE).** Rationale: portable-pty's handles are blocking, so the pump needs threads either way. `hook` spawns once per hook event and must not pay for runtime startup. rmcp and interprocess-async require Tokio, so it is confined to the subcommand that uses them. CI enforces this with a sole-root `cargo deny` `tokio` ban (`deny-sync.toml`, run once per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt`), evaluated for the Windows, macOS and Linux target triples, plus a `cargo check` of the listed sync crates on all three OSes (CI job 3). `viola-channel`, whose optional `tokio` feature `viola-mcp` enables, is not on that list (since chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): its normal graph without the feature is proven tokio-free by `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` in the same CI supply-chain step.

subject: dec-pty
text:
- **[PTY] portable-pty `=0.8.1` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill).** Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF, because ConPTY does not close the output stream on exit. If 0.8.1's Windows `kill()` misbehaves, the fallback is `TerminateProcess` on `child.process_id()` via windows-sys. The host stdin handed to the pump is `viola_pty::host_stdin()`: on Windows with a console stdin it is viola's own reader calling `ReadConsoleW` (no Ctrl-Z wakeup control; UTF-16 → UTF-8, a split surrogate carried, every `0x1A` kept, a 0-unit read read again), because std's console stdin drops a read's trailing `0x1A` and ends input on a lone `^Z` — source-read at the pinned toolchain and as measured on `windows-2025` (ci#37226294797, `tui_ctrl_z…` green); elsewhere, and for a redirected Windows stdin, it is `std::io::stdin()`. Its callers are `run`'s pump and the fake agent. Rationale: 0.8.1 is spike-proven (S1, O1 render stress, the Pulse live test, and about an hour driving this arch session in Windows Terminal with no PTY defect). 0.9.0 is excluded because of the Windows garbage-read bug wezterm#6783. Swap triggers: portable-pty-psmux 0.9.7 if the O1 stray-spaces artifact reproduces only under `viola run` (then test `PASSTHROUGH_MODE`). An own ConPTY on windows-sys 0.61.2 + nix 0.31.3 comes only after a measured defect the seam cannot absorb. As built (chunk 2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows, measured on the Windows host in its research facts 1-5): `viola run` puts its own host terminal into raw input + VT output for the run through `HostTerminal` (Windows console modes; Unix termios) and restores the saved modes on Drop — without it ConPTY line-buffers keys until Enter and swallows Ctrl-C; off a terminal it is a no-op.
 The child's cwd is set explicitly to viola's current directory (portable-pty 0.8.1 defaults to `%USERPROFILE%`). A revived start has the one other source: `viola revive` sets the child's cwd to the instance snapshot's recorded `cwd`, the directory the first start spawned its child in. It reads that value only after the strict-modes check on the instance's files, and it must name an existing directory, else the revive is refused `cwd-missing`. Program resolution and the version gate never read the recorded directory: the program is looked up on the reviving process's own `PATH`, from its own current directory (a boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-10, after it was shown to him as one, the overseer and the operator as relay; chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive). viola resolves the child program to an absolute path itself (portable-pty's Windows search tries the exact name first and hits the extensionless npm sh shim). The pump keeps the ConPTY input writer until the child exits, because dropping it makes conhost send `CTRL_CLOSE` to the child (exit `0xC000013A`). The exit is recorded as `exit_source` `handle-wait` or `kill-fallback`. As measured (chunk 2026-09-29-h2-conpty-resize-probe, H2): a key written through the seam right after `resize` returned can fail to reach the child — on the windows-2025 runner (image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260922.246.2), in an isolated loop of the viola-pty red test under `cargo llvm-cov nextest`, 13 of 200 iterations lost it (ci#36527891850), every loss the same class: the child's key-free size watcher saw the new size, viola's writer wrote and flushed the key, and the Rust test child blocked in its console read never received it; ConPTY wrote no cursor-position request (`dsr-cpr 0` on every loss, and on the dev host, Windows 10.0.26200.9457 / conhost 10.0.26100.8875, which read 20/20).
 The measured span runs from the ConPTY input-pipe write to that test child's console read; where inside it the key is lost is not established (an overseer read of microsoft/terminal's current source, relayed at that chunk's wrap, found no input-buffer flush on the resize path — a relay, not verified here). Whether the real `claude` (Node/libuv, `ReadConsoleInputW`) loses a key typed right after a resize is unmeasured; the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements" owns that measurement, blocked on an interactive Windows host (the harness's local `run --local-live`, a real-`claude` `viola verify`, does not claim it), and the founder's product question on H2 stays open. viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize ([Human Takeover / Wheel]). A test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first (0 of 200 lost, ci#36529038462). As built (chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty, founder ruling 2026-09-29): on Windows x64 the child's ConPTY is Microsoft's current one, sideloaded. Every `viola` process, in every role, restricts its DLL search to System32 as the second statement of `main` (`viola_pty::sideload::restrict_dll_search`, process-wide and one-way), so a bare-name load never picks a `conpty.dll` planted in the CWD or on `PATH`. `run` pins the embedded `conpty.dll` + `OpenConsole.exe` into `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/` ([Deployment / Distribution]) and pre-loads `conpty.dll` by absolute path (`viola_pty::sideload::preload`: a relative path is refused, the module is never freed), so portable-pty `=0.8.1`'s own bare-name `LoadLibraryW("conpty.dll")` returns that module and the child is hosted by the pinned `OpenConsole.exe`; the seam and portable-pty are unchanged, and viola-pty knows no pinned path.
 `viola_pty::pty_backend()` reports `conpty-sideload` after a successful pre-load, else `conpty` (Windows) or `openpty`. An absent, tampered, unreadable or unloadable sideload, or one whose `conpty/` directory or a companion fails its owner/DACL check ([Deployment / Distribution]), fails open to kernel32's inbox ConPTY with no byte, refusal or exit change (`sideload_fallback` on `process-start`). Spawners outside `viola run` stay on the inbox ConPTY: the harness `supervise::spawn_in_pty`, root `tests/support/outer_pty.rs` and viola-pty's own tests. H2 with and without, measured in one run on the windows-2025 runner (image `windows-2025-vs2026` 20260828.587, ci#36563868040, the measurement-only race of the pre-`dce98ad` shape, 200 iterations each): sideloaded 0 of 200 lost, inbox 14 of 200 lost — beside the inbox 13 of 200 above; no rate is claimed. The sideloaded host writes a different spawn preamble, `ESC[1t ESC[c ESC[?1004h ESC[?9001h` (the inbox one: `ESC[?9001h ESC[?1004h`), and its DA1 query `ESC[c` holds the child's start until something answers it — as measured at the chunk's `evidence/da1-stall.md` on the dev host, 3.54 s unanswered on pipes vs 0.54 s answered (0.48 s on the inbox host); a terminal answers it, and the answer travels through viola's pump, so the child's start now waits for the pump. viola stays silent (it never answers DA1 itself); the stall of a `viola run` with no terminal on its stdio is an open product finding, owned by the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements", blocked on an interactive Windows host.

subject: dec-database-state-store
text:
- **[Database / State Store] ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots + std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files (KEYSTONE).** Each event line is written with one `write` call. The next append heals a torn last line; readers count it and never rewrite the log. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state): every appender (`append_event`, `append_event_at`, `try_append_event`) reads the log's last byte under the lock it already holds and, when the log is not empty and that byte is not LF, writes one LF and its line in a single write. The line then starts on a fresh line, no earlier byte moves, and every offset handed out before still starts the same line; `append_event_at` hands its builder and returns the offset its line really starts at (L + 1 after a heal, L otherwise). The healing process logs one `state-recovered` line, and an append that did not heal logs none. The one reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `replay::session_chain`, the pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at start, `LinkSet::restore`, one pass from offset 0, and since chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::log_pass`, one pass from offset 0 per scanned instance whose snapshot read or was absent) counts what it steps over, per read, as `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`: a line whose `kind` it does not know is not returned (`link` and `unlink` are known kinds since that chunk, returned and no longer counted); a known-kind line with a top-level key outside the six, or a `data` key outside its kind's list, is returned and counted once; an over-long line, a terminated line that is not one JSON object and the unterminated last line of the read count as torn, the last still neither returned nor rewritten.
 The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. The wheel is decided in the wrapper's memory and mirrored to a snapshot. Budget readings are timestamped, last-writer-wins, under `File::lock`. Rationale: the audit trail stays human-readable and `tail`-able, there is no C in the build, and there is no daemon to serialise writers. SQLite (C build, binary format) and redb (multi-process mode hardened only 2026-09-06) were rejected. Lock files are separate from logs because append + exclusive lock fails on Windows (rust-lang/rust#54118). Upgrade path if a real query need appears: a derived, rebuildable SQLite index (rusqlite) beside the authoritative log. The log stays the source of truth.

subject: dec-snapshot-writer
text:
- **[Snapshot writer] tempfile 3.27.0 `persist` through ONE shared helper.** `viola_state::fs::replace_private` creates the temp file beside the target, sets its mode before any byte is written (0600, or 0700 for the pinned `viola`), writes, `sync_all`s and `persist`s; a failure leaves the target as it was. On Windows a `persist` refused with raw OS error 5 (a reader holding the target open, as measured at chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events research.md M1 under every share mode) is retried every 10 ms, re-persisting the same temp file, at most `viola_state::fs::REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` = 100 attempts (an attempt count, never a time bound); any other error returns at once. The loop sits in the private `replace_private_retrying`, which takes the decision to retry a failed rename (from its raw OS error) from its caller; `replace_private_with` passes `retry_replace(_, HOST_IS_WINDOWS)`, so the product's behaviour is the one above and the loop's attempt bound is exercised by a unit case on every host (chunk 2026-10-13-epoch-4-survivors). `replace_private_shared` is the variant for files every concurrent start of one version writes identically (the pinned copy, the plugin files, the Windows x64 ConPTY companions under `bin/<version>-<hash>/conpty/`): a replace that fails counts as done when the target already holds exactly those bytes. The companions' held open (`FILE_SHARE_READ` only) retries a Win32 error 32 (sharing violation) under the same `REPLACE_ATTEMPTS` bound (`retry_open`, `open_held_waiting`), as measured at chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty: two concurrent first starts, the refusal lasting 5-11 ms after the other start's write, 0 of 6 pairs over companions already written. No call site carries its own temp + rename code.
 Rationale: atomic-write-file 0.3.1 was the first choice, but its licence is BSD-3-Clause, outside `deny.toml`'s allow list (operator ruling at the 2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order plan); tempfile was already locked, MIT OR Apache-2.0.

subject: dec-hook-transport
text:
- **[Hook Transport] Exec-form `command` hooks: `"command": "<pinned viola copy>", "args": ["hook", "<event>"]`.** Tiers:
  - sync with a decision: PreToolUse with matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`, plus PermissionRequest.
  - sync with no reply body (the ordering spine): SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop. Each writes its `hook.event` and exits 0 within viola's spine deadline: one built-in value for every event, below the `timeout` (5 s) those hooks get in `hooks.json`. That value is the product constant `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` = 1 s, the bound the perf gate reads (test-plan §10). The connect deadline `viola hook` passes to `Client::connect_by` is the hook-local, crate-private `CONNECT_DEADLINE` = 750 ms (provisional), asserted below `SPINE_DEADLINE` by a unit test. If the endpoint cannot be reached or written within the deadline, the hook records the failure in `diagnostics/` and exits 0. The event is lost rather than the turn delayed, and a driver recovers through `wait`'s `timeout_ms`.
  - SessionEnd: sync within viola's own ~1 s budget: the channel under the same provisional 750 ms `CONNECT_DEADLINE`, else, once the instance check has passed ([Hook Contract]) and the endpoint is not reached or its server check fails, a direct `try_lock` append (`viola_state::try_append_event` with `Source::Hook`, which writes nothing while `events.ndjson.lock` is held), else nothing; `hooks.json` gives it no `timeout` key. `run` writes `session-end` from the process exit if no hook arrived.
  - `async: true`, printing nothing: Notification, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure.

  Rationale: exec form skips Git Bash path rewriting and shell startup. `http` hooks need a fixed URL, which means a central listener and so a daemon. `mcp_tool` is unavailable at SessionStart. The 1.5 s SessionEnd budget is never raised. The tier map is itself a ledger row that `viola verify` re-stamps.

subject: dec-hook-contract
text:
- **[Hook Contract] Hooks fail open.** Exit 0 with a JSON body is a decision. Exit 0 with no body is no decision (the `unverified-cli` degrade: the dialog renders for the human). Exit 2 is never produced. `hook` exits 0 at once when `VIOLA_NAME` is absent. The one exception is the hidden `hook <event> --capture <DIR> [--answers <DIR>]` arm, which only `viola verify`'s probe plugins call, and its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]`, which only Run B's probe settings call (it files the payload as `StatusLine.<k>.json` under the same claim and write, beside `StatusLine.<k>.shell` holding exactly `bin-sh` when the word equals `/bin/sh` byte for byte, else `other`, the word itself written nowhere; nothing printed; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, «Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`): it reads no `VIOLA_*`, does no obs init and opens no channel; it takes an absolute, existing `<DIR>`, reads stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and claims `<DIR>/<PascalEvent>.<k>.json` exclusively — create-new at 0600 (`viola_state::fs::create_private_new`) from the first free `k`, the next `k` on `AlreadyExists`, then the raw bytes through `replace_private` over its own claim, so two concurrent captures never share a name (`k` counts across events, so names sort in arrival order). `--answers <DIR>` is read only with `--capture` (inert without it): for a dialog event, the event's ordinal `j` in claim order selects `<DIR>/<Event>.<j>`, read through `take(64)` as an exact closed `ProbeAnswer` id, and `ledger::probe_body` builds the body from the filed payload through `dialog::decision_body` alone — one write to stdout, the probe's dialogs answered by the hook, never by a key.
 Any failure prints and writes nothing; stderr is always empty and the exit always 0 (the capture arm a boundary widening ratified live by the founder, 2026-09-28 20:24:32; its `--answers` body the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05, relayed by the overseer). A sync dialog hook (`viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request`) waits on `hook.dialog` for at most the instance's dialog hold, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`: whole seconds from 60 to 3600, default 60 (`viola_core::DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX`, PROVISIONAL, beside `SPINE_DEADLINE`), a `DialogHold` read once at the wrapper's start; the hook bounds its reply read at the ceiling, `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s), never at each start's hold, and writes stdout once. The dialog hooks' `timeout` in the embedded `hooks.json` is 3615 s, above the ceiling by a margin a test pins, so viola, never Claude Code, ends the wait, and the rendered plugin stays byte-identical across starts. At the hold's end the wrapper replies `null`: the hook exits 0 with no body and the dialog renders for the human. The wrapper then clears the pending `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. `hook` never writes to stderr. Its codes-only process log goes to the home-level `diagnostics/hook-<name>.ndjson`, and content-bearing detail goes only to the instance's `diagnostics/detail-hook.ndjson` (format owned by obs). A failure to write either is ignored. Rationale: exit 2 is a blocking error in Claude Code's contract, and a viola bug must never block the user's session.

subject: dec-budget-governor
text:
- **[Budget Governor] Soft stop at the turn boundary.** Once a configured threshold is crossed (defaults `five_hour` ≥ 90 %, `seven_day` ≥ 85 %), automated `send` is refused with `budget-paused` through the same refusal path as `human-typing`. Human keys are never blocked, and a running turn finishes. The pause lifts when `resets_at` passes or on `viola release --budget`. `release --budget` leaves the wheel where it is, and a plain `release` returns the wheel to `driver` without lifting a budget pause. `release --budget` is sent to one instance's wrapper and lifts the pause for that instance only, until the crossed window's `resets_at` passes, so the next over-threshold reading does not re-pause it. The wrapper evaluates its gate from `budget.json`, read under `budget.json.lock`, at three points: at start, when a `send` arrives, and at each `turn-ended`. It never polls. A crossed threshold, a passed `resets_at` or an expired override takes effect at the next of these points, and only then is `budget-gate` appended. So a snapshot can still read `budget_paused: true` after the reset, until a `send` arrives or a turn ends, and every surface that shows the snapshot inherits that. The wrapper mirrors its budget-pause state, including any override, to the instance snapshot, where `list` reads it. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor; `src/run/budget.rs`, one `BudgetGate` per wrapper, no thread and no timer): a window is crossed only when its `used_percentage` is known and at or above its threshold and its `resets_at` is known, parses as RFC 3339 and is later than now, so a window whose `resets_at` is `"unknown"`, unparseable or passed never pauses. With both windows crossed the refusal names `five-hour`.
 The `send` point sits after the text refusals and the first `human-typing` read and before the running-turn read, so the order is `control-character` → `empty-text` → `human-typing` → `budget-paused` → `turn-running` → the readiness gate's wait; the gate is read once per `send`, never again after that wait. `answer`, `wait`, `last`, `pause` and `hook.dialog` do not read the gate (read in the diff: its five product call sites; since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the root case `path6_a_closed_gate_leaves_answer_wait_last_and_pause_alone`, `tests/cli_budget.rs`, drives `answer`, `wait`, `last` and `pause` under one closed gate, each giving the exit code and the document it gives under an open one; no case drives `hook.dialog` under a closed gate). An override covers both windows until its end and is dropped at the next point after that end. It does not outlive its wrapper: every start, a revived one included, evaluates from `budget.json` alone and restores none. `release --budget` with no pause standing records nothing. `budget-gate` is appended, and the snapshot's `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` are rewritten, only when the triple (paused, window, override end) changes, both before the evaluation returns; a record that cannot land is an error and the recorded state stays as it was. The thresholds are read once, at the wrapper's start, and no value of either switches the gate off. The gate is fail-open: no reading, an `"unknown"` figure, a passed or unparseable `resets_at`, an unreadable or refused `budget.json` and a bad threshold each leave it open or at its default. The decision takes the wall-clock instant as an argument (no clock seam). With figures missing, viola uses the newest reading from any wrapped session and shows its age. With no reading at all it records `unknown` and does not block.
 The statusline is wrapped only for sessions started by `viola run`, through a per-session settings override that then runs the user's own statusline command unchanged. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through) the wrap is Unix only: on Windows no override is written and no command is run, and that half is owed to the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements" (the founder's word on the cut, live, 2026-10-10, relayed verbatim by the operator). A reading is recorded only when the payload holds `rate_limits`. Rationale: the per-model weekly window is hidden (claude-code#91920), so thresholds are set low. The user's global statusline config is never touched, and a visible, conservative governor supports the "ordinary individual usage" posture.

subject: dec-cli-version-compatibility
text:
- **[CLI Version Compatibility] Per-behaviour capability ledger + transport-only degrade + `viola verify` re-stamp.** Ledger rows:
  - S3: AskUserQuestion via PreToolUse `updatedInput`.
  - S7: ExitPlanMode approves only through PreToolUse, as `allow` + `updatedInput` set to the tool's own input, unchanged (a non-object input gives `{}`); revise via `deny` + `message`. A bare `allow` left the plan dialog up on live 2.1.288 (the founder's live ruling after step 0's STOP 7, 2026-10-05).
  - S8: free text and `annotations`.
  - The R8 identity floor: the measured `CLAUDE*` parent-identity names stripped even when the persistent environment defines them (every other `CLAUDE*` name follows the prefix rule, see Occupied Resources → Environment variables).
  - npm-shim → `claude.exe` resolution.
  - Statusline `rate_limits.*`, the settings-override mechanism, and the shell Claude Code runs a statusline command through on each OS. Rows `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits` since chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, relied only where the status line is wrapped (`statusline::WRAPPED_HERE`, Unix): on Unix the statusline pass-through and, since chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor, the budget gate's `budget-paused` refusal rest on stamped rows; the Windows legs are owed to "Windows-only live measurements" (§Cross-cutting Patterns, Capability ledger).
  - Harness prompt prefixes: `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message`, `<cross-session-message` (compiled, matched on the raw start). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/scratch-session.md`): a real cross-session message reaches UserPromptSubmit unescaped, as `<cross-session-message from="…" from-name="…" from-mode="…">`, a newline, the text, a newline and `</cross-session-message>`, and the plain prefix files it `harness`; a `<task-notification>` typed at the very start of a prompt arrives as typed, so a human who types it first is filed `harness` (see Tag escaping). The escaped cross-session form rests on a relayed measurement alone (overseer1's F115 on andromeda-worker, the viola-lab prototype's `harness_injected`); it was not seen in that session and stays compiled. On the CLI the builder session itself runs (PATH `claude`, read by counts only, the same chunk's `evidence/harness-prompts-driver-log.md`) the `<agent-message from=` and `<task-notification>` forms reach the hook starting at the tag, with no preface. These readings came from a scratch probe, not a `viola verify` probe, so the harness-prefix ledger row stays owed.
  - The long-paste wrapper (row `long-paste-wrapper`): the CLI's own pair arrives unescaped, `<pasted_content id="X">\n…\n</pasted_content id="X">`, the close repeating the id (981 bytes wrapped, 749 not, on 2.1.280; the close form as measured at chunk 2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events research.md M5), and the CLI frames it: two newlines directly before the open tag and, after the close tag, one newline at the prompt's end, two when typed text follows, and three in all between two adjacent pairs. The lone-paste frame is as measured on 2.1.287 in four live sessions at chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows (`evidence/step0-shapes.md`, `rehearsal-shapes.md`, `record-round-green.md`: a 1 500-byte one-line paste wrapped, a 200-byte paste not); the frame beside typed text and between two pairs is as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host (`evidence/scratch-session.md`). The id is 4 hex characters: every pair of one session carried the same id, the two pairs of one prompt included, and it differed between sessions (as measured at the same two chunks). `viola-agent-claude` (`hook::unwrap_pastes`) unwraps only that exact same-id pair and removes that frame with it, nothing wider: the two newlines before the open tag, the one after the close, and a second after the close when text follows that is not the next pair's own two-newline frame. A third newline before, a second after at the prompt's end and a lone one before stay, an open tag with no matching close removes nothing, and everything else outside a pair is kept byte for byte.
 A pasted text's own last newline never reaches the hook (as measured at the 2026-10-07 chunk, `evidence/scratch-session.md`, `live-shape-red-green.md`): for a wrapped text that ends in a newline the CLI adds none before the close tag, so its prompt is byte for byte that of the same text without the newline, and an unwrapped text loses its last newline too; `text` is then the pasted text less that newline. The measurement stands and no `send` relies on it: `send` never types a text that ends in a newline ([Delivery Confirmation]). The frame beside typed text and between two pairs is compiled on that one measurement and held by `hook.rs` unit cases only: no `viola verify` run types those shapes (Run B pastes each compiled text alone), so the `long-paste-wrapper` row re-validates only the lone-paste frame per CLI version. No probe is owed for them: a shape no `send` relies on needs no probe (the founder's live ruling on the ledger rule, 2026-10-07T11:37Z, relayed by the overseer). They arise only when a human types beside a paste, so no claim and no wheel decision rests on them; after a CLI change a human's own prompt `text` may carry a stray newline until it is noticed. Read statically from the 2.1.287 binary, not measured: the wrap threshold (over 800 characters or more than 2 lines) and the feature flag behind the wrapping. Unmeasured: a long or a repeated text pasted while the paste hint stands.
  - Modal and input-box screen signatures.
  - The hook tier map.
  - Turn end without Stop: which hook, if any, fires when a turn ends on an API error (Stop does not fire on a user interrupt), so the running-turn state can be cleared.
  - Dialog concurrency: whether two dialog hooks (PreToolUse `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`, PermissionRequest) can be open at once in one session, for example on parallel tool calls.
  - `claude agents --json` join field (row `agents-join`): a row exposes both the child pid (`pid`) and the session id (`sessionId`) that match a wrapped instance, as measured on 2.1.287 (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board: the record round's `agents-join` pass, `stamped 2.1.287  23 pass  0 fail`, on the Linux dev host; its Windows reading owed on "Windows-only live measurements"). The row is relied on every OS and probed by Run B's one agents read (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 1 of that chunk, `inputs#I1`, relayed verbatim by the operator).
  - Local commands: built-in local commands fire no UserPromptSubmit (measured: `/remote-control`), so the ledger lists each known local command with its delivery post-condition or "none" (compiled, `ledger::LOCAL_COMMANDS`). For `/clear` it is a SessionStart with source `clear` and a new `session_id` (row `local-command-clear`): as measured on 2.1.287 in `viola verify`'s Run B (chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, `evidence/rehearsal-shapes.md`), a pasted `/clear` fires SessionEnd (`reason` `clear`), then SessionStart (`source` `clear`, a new `session_id`, no `model` key), and no UserPromptSubmit. `/remote-control` has no measured post-condition today and no probe types it (it would open a remote-control link). `/compact` (listed since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows) has the post-condition a SessionStart with source `compact` and the session's own `session_id` (row `local-command-compact`): as measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host in `viola verify`'s Run B (chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row, `evidence/live-round.md`), a pasted `/compact` fires a SessionStart (`source` `compact`, Run B's first `session_id`) and no UserPromptSubmit, its answer read 21 413 ms after the paste; its confirm window is `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL) beside the 10 s `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK`, so a `send` of it is confirmed on a verified CLI and `unconfirmable` at once only on an unverified one. Whether the CLI fires a SessionEnd before that SessionStart is not measured. Skills are not local commands: they expand into a prompt and fire UserPromptSubmit (measured: `/andromeda-arch`).
  - Tag escaping (row `tag-escaping`): the CLI inserts a backslash after `<` in a `pasted_content` tag the user typed, so a literal `<pasted_content` arrives in UserPromptSubmit as `<\pasted_content` and a typed close as `<\/pasted_content`. As measured on 2.1.287, mid-text (chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, `evidence/step0-shapes.md`), only those two tags were escaped: a typed `<task-notification>` in the middle of a prompt arrived as typed. At the start-of-prompt position, the one the harness classification reads, it arrives as typed too (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/scratch-session.md`), so a human who types it first is filed `harness`. `viola-agent-claude` classifies `harness` on the raw prefix first, then removes any long-paste wrapper with its frame, then un-escapes `<\` before an ASCII letter or `/` when it normalises `prompt-submitted`, so a typed pair is never unwrapped and delivery matching compares plain text. An escaped tag is typed text and never classifies `harness`, with one exception: `<\cross-session-message` is a harness prefix, on the relayed measurement that the cross-session message arrives escaped, `<\cross-session-message from="…" from-name="…">`, as the CLI's own injection — a human who types that tag at a prompt's start is filed `harness` too (founder-ratified, 2026-09-29). On 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host the message arrived unescaped (Harness prompt prefixes above); the escaped form was not seen there and its prefix stays compiled.

  `viola run` learns the CLI version by running the resolved child executable once with `--version` (no user args, stdout and stderr drained through `MAX_FRAME`, killed at 5 s) before spawning it; the first line must read exactly `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`. Output it cannot parse counts as an unlisted version. The fake agent answers `--version` the same way. A version is verified only when its stamp holds every relied row `pass` (`LedgerRow::relied()`, below); `cli_verified` (and `cli_version` when parsed) is recorded in the snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`. On an unverified version viola still types, runs the wheel and emits events, but withholds dialog answers, and drivers get `unverified-cli`. As landed by chunk 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify and widened by chunks 2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes, 2026-10-05-dialog-rows-and-re-probe, 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row, 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows and 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, the ledger (`viola_agent_claude::ledger`, a closed set) holds twenty-four rows (the members of `LedgerRow::ALL`, in its order): `shim-resolution` · `spine-hooks` · `session-start-fields` · `prompt-verbatim` · `stop-message` · `largest-hook-payload` · `modal-signature` · `input-box-signature` · `quiet-period` · `confirm-window` · `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency` · `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear` · `paste-newline` · `statusline-override` · `statusline-shell` · `statusline-rate-limits` · `resume-session` · `agents-join` · `local-command-compact`.
 The relied set is `LedgerRow::relied()`, `ALL` filtered in its order by `relied_on(row, statusline::WRAPPED_HERE)`: the three statusline rows are relied only where the status line is wrapped (Unix), so a Unix host relies on all twenty-four rows and a Windows host on twenty-one, the first eighteen, `resume-session`, `agents-join` and `local-command-compact`, the last three relied on every OS.
 `check(row, &Probes)` reads `Probes { print, typed, trusted, dialogs, statusline, resumed, agents }` (`trusted`: Run B's captures in claim order; `statusline`: Run B's status line captures in `k` order; `resumed`: Run E's captures in claim order; `agents`: Run B's one agents capture, an `AgentsCapture`): the `agents-join` row passes only when that capture parses and holds exactly one row whose `pid` is Run B's child pid, whose `sessionId` is the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture and whose status is idle or busy (`agents_joined`), and fails with no capture; the override row passes on at least one capture, the shell row on at least one capture whose every shell verdict is `bin-sh`, and the rate-limits row on a capture whose `rate_limits.five_hour` and `.seven_day` each hold an integer `used_percentage` 0–100 and an integer `resets_at` (`whole_rate_limits`, narrower than `statusline::reading`, which also takes an RFC 3339 string and a fraction), and the resume row only when Run E's first SessionStart capture has `source` `resume` and the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, taken only when `is_session_id` accepts it (`ledger::resume_target`), and the compact row only when the first SessionStart capture of source `compact` after the newline turn's prompt (`compact_start`) has a non-empty `session_id` equal to that of Run B's first SessionStart capture, no UserPromptSubmit carries `/compact`, and `compact_latency_ms` is within `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (`local_command_compacted`); a run that raised no dialog fails its dialog rows, and a Run B that did not paste a text fails that text's row.
 `viola verify [--record <DIR>] [-- <program> [args…]]` (program default `claude`) first drives ONE print-mode probe, `<program> -p "<PROBE_PROMPT>" --model haiku --plugin-dir <probe>/plugin --no-session-persistence` (cwd the probe dir, 120 s deadline), whose `viola-verify-probe` plugin captures the four spine payloads through the hidden `hook --capture` arm. It then drives five interactive PTY runs (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs` and its children under `src/cmd/verify/typed/`). Each is a direct spawn under the R8 strip at a fixed 80×24, its output capped at `MAX_FRAME` into a `Screen` fed under `catch_unwind`. Run A runs untrusted in a fresh 0700 `viola-verify-*` dir under the OS temp dir, with empty input, and is ended by a kill. Once Run B's first turn has settled, before its framing pastes, verify makes ONE `claude agents --json` read (`typed::turns::agents_read`: Run B's program, cwd the probe dir, the R8 strip, `VERSION_DEADLINE`, none once a stop is read), its capture carried in memory and never written to the captures dir, its spawn pair `agents-probe`; no live start is added (a widening of verify's child set the founder ratified himself, his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`, relayed verbatim by the operator); in CI the fake agent's `agents` mode answers it. Run B runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/` (0700, a drop guard).
 On a wrapped OS (Unix), and only for shell-plain paths, it also gets one `--settings <probe dir>/typed/statusline.json` after its `--plugin-dir` pair (`typed::runs::trusted_args`; the document `statusline::probe_document` builds, written 0600; Windows passes none), whose `statusLine` command `<pinned viola> hook statusline --capture <probe dir>/typed/statusline --shell "$0"` files each status line payload with its shell verdict through the hidden capture arm ([Hook Contract]); Runs A, C and D keep their arguments and no run is added (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, «Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`). It gets six bracketed pastes, all compiled texts: `PROBE_PROMPT`, then `PROBE_LONG_PASTE` (1 500 bytes, one line), `PROBE_TAG_PASTE` (200 bytes), `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (113 bytes, ASCII, exactly one LF at neither end, no CR), `PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND` (the list's `/compact`) and `PROBE_LOCAL_COMMAND` (the list's `/clear`), each of the five added ones only into rows that hold an input-box literal and no modal literal, none after the stop, each text waited for one more UserPromptSubmit and one more Stop, and each local command for one more SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit, up to `PROBE_DEADLINE` (`ledger::FRAMING_TURNS`, in paste order `paste-1` · `paste-2` · `paste-3` · `compact-1` · `clear-1`); a failed wait ends the added pastes, and verify still makes six starts. The long, tag-like and local-command pastes are the founder's live answer of 2026-10-06T19:38Z, given after the widening was shown, relayed by the overseer. The newline paste is his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row («Пятая вставка в Run B», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I2`).
 The `/compact` paste is his own answer to P4 fork 1 of chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row («Шестая вставка в Run B», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I3`). It is ended by Ctrl-C, Ctrl-C again after 500 ms, then a kill at `PROBE_DEADLINE`; a run stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`cmd::verify::stop`) is ended by a kill with no key, starts no later run and writes no stamp. Each screen settles at the first `QUIET_PERIOD`-quiet instant holding a compiled literal, else at the first quiet instant past `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, with one exception: after each of Run B's added text turns (the long, the tag-like and the newline turns) and after its `/compact` turn (the rows `/clear` is pasted into) the rows the paste guard reads come from a wait (`Run::box_wait`) that ends only on a `QUIET_PERIOD`-quiet screen holding a compiled literal, on a poisoned screen, or at `PROBE_DEADLINE` from that turn's Stop, so a quiet screen with no literal keeps waiting past `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (the founder's live answer of 2026-10-06T20:49Z, relayed by the overseer). The reason is measured: after a long paste 2.1.287's footer reads `paste again to expand` and holds no input-box literal for 8.0 s from the paste, which was 6.5 s after that turn's Stop (chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows, `evidence/rehearsal-shapes.md`). Verify's `box_wait` is its own wait, bounded by `PROBE_DEADLINE`. The readiness gate of `viola run` ([Screen Model]) waits on the same screen too, up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT` from the send's entry into the gate: since chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint, on a verified CLI a `send` issued while the hint stands (a quiet screen with no compiled literal) is delivered once the input box returns, and a hint that outlasts the bound ends `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed.
 Both are as measured at that chunk: the delivery under the fake agent's 3 000 ms hold (`evidence/hint-red-green.md`), the refusal at the bound on the injected clock in unit cases only. A `send` under the real CLI's hint is as measured on live 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (`evidence/live-readings.ndjson`, `send-under-hint`): a 32-byte text sent 4 248 ms after a 2 564-byte long paste was issued waited in the gate, was issued 8 319 ms after the paste, and was confirmed (`send-confirmed.duration_ms` 4 081 against the 8 500 ms bound), with no `wheel` record. Before that chunk such a `send` was refused at the first quiet instant, 0.63 s after it was issued on the real CLI (as measured on 2.1.287 at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host, `evidence/hint-window.md`, and under the fake agent at chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes, `evidence/paste-hint-send.md`). The same sequence without the hint was and is delivered. On the real CLI the hint is a timer of 8.0 s from the last long paste (nine timings over the two chunks, 8.000 s to 8.023 s; a second long paste restarts it, a short one does not), 3.8 s to 7.0 s of it after the turn's Stop. A `viola wait` with no cursor issued in the window woke on nothing and ran to its deadline, and `wait --after` the earlier cursor returns the logged turn end at once, inside the window, so the advice of the `input-not-ready` hint line of that time (`viola wait <name>, then send again`) did not lead out of it; the line no longer gives that advice (below). On an unverified CLI the partial gate typed a short text under the hint and the CLI submitted and confirmed it; a long or a repeated text under the hint is unmeasured.
 What `send` does while the hint stands is the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-07T10:29Z (relayed by the overseer), built at chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint: on a verified CLI the gate waits for the input box on a quiet screen with no literal, and the bound is 8.5 s. The fake agent's hold cap rose to 10 000 ms with it. The `input-not-ready` hint line is no longer printed for the paste-hint cause. Its wording for the remaining causes (a modal, a screen that never goes quiet, a poisoned screen, a hint past the bound) is the founder's, landed at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (`send_hint`, `src/human/hints.rs`): `<name> was not ready for input; send again, and if it repeats a human must look at the session`, in place of the line that advised `viola wait`. Exit code, refusal, detail and `--json` did not change. The moved bound was re-verified by path on 2.1.287 at that chunk (`stamped 2.1.287  17 pass  0 fail`, `evidence/reverify-round.md`). Run C runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-dialogs/` with `--model haiku --settings <DIALOG_SETTINGS>` (an `ask` rule for `Bash(touch viola-probe-permission)`) and the dialog-kind probe plugin, and pastes the three compiled dialog prompts, each after the previous turn's Stop capture; its one `allow` runs that `touch` inside its own dir. Run D runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-plan/` with `--model haiku --permission-mode plan --settings {"plansDirectory":"<Run D dir>/plans"}` (a 0700 `plans/` inside the 0700 dir, so the plan file lands inside the run's own dir and none under `~/.claude/plans`, as measured on 2.1.288 and 2.1.287) and the dialog plugin, and pastes `PLAN_PROMPT`.
 Runs C and D wait for the input box with no modal before any paste; their dialogs are answered only by the probe hook's `--answers` body from the compiled answer table `PROBE_ANSWERS`; after the last Stop is captured the screen settles, as Run B's turn does (a 300 ms quiet grace, not an absolute guarantee), and the run is ended by a kill; each wait is bounded by `PROBE_DEADLINE`. Run E runs last, after Run D (the founder's own answer to P4 fork 2 of chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows, «Run E, шестой старт», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`): it reads Run B's captures and takes the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart through `ledger::resume_target` (only of the session-id shape; with none it spawns nothing and the row fails), and runs trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/` (0700, a drop guard) with the run args, then `--plugin-dir` and the capture plugin under `<probe dir>/resume/`, then `viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)` (`--resume <id>`), with empty input and no `--settings`; it waits for one SessionStart capture up to `PROBE_DEADLINE`, settles after it and is ended by a kill. As measured on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/live-round.md`), the CLI found Run B's session from Run E's own `-resume` project directory. No run writes a byte into a CLI dialog, and a start showing a modal is killed with no key (the founder's live rulings of 2026-10-05, relayed by the overseer).
 It checks the relied rows (`check_rows` walks `LedgerRow::relied()`), prints one stdout step line per relied row (`[NN/MM] <row id> <row words>  pass|fail`, `MM` being `LedgerRow::relied().len()`: 24 on Unix, the last `[24/24] local-command-compact …`; 21 on Windows, the last `[21/21] local-command-compact …`) and a `stamped <ver>  N pass  M fail` summary, and writes the stamps through the one writer (the Ledger stamps envelope, Standard Contracts); a failing row still writes its stamp, and verify exits 1. `--record <DIR>` writes the scrubbed `<DIR>/<ver>/<Event>.default.json` fixtures, the dialog captures as `<Event>.<stem>-<n>.json` variants (`ledger::dialog_variants`), Run B's framing captures as `UserPromptSubmit.paste-<n>.json`, `SessionStart.compact-<n>.json`, `SessionEnd.clear-<n>.json` and `SessionStart.clear-<n>.json` variants (`ledger::framing_variants`), Run B's status line captures as `StatusLine.default-1.json` and `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` (`ledger::statusline_variants`: the first capture without `rate_limits`, the first that passes the rate-limits row), Run E's first SessionStart as `SessionStart.resume-1.json` (`ledger::resume_variants`), Run B's agents read as `Agents.recorded-1.json` (Run B's own row only, `ledger::agents_variant`) and the signature-only `Screen.<phase>.json` screens the fake agent replays, only when 0 rows fail. An unclean recording is refused whole, naming the file and the check code, never the content (Occupied Resources → Repository). The other rows above land with their owning chunks, each with its own typed or live probe.
 The long-paste wrapper, tag escaping and the `/clear` local-command row landed with chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-and-paste-framing-rows through Run B's typed probe; the `paste-newline` row (an LF typed inside a bracketed paste stays inside the one prompt submitted) landed with chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row through Run B's newline paste, checked by `pasted(&probes.trusted, PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE)` (the first trusted-run UserPromptSubmit whose prompt normalises to the whole text, so a CLI that submitted at the LF leaves no such capture), as measured on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/live-round.md`: one prompt equal to the 113-byte text byte for byte, `stamped 2.1.287  18 pass  0 fail`; one round, five starts), not measured on Windows (owed to "Windows-only live measurements"); the `resume-session` row (`claude --resume <id>` reopens the session under that id, which `viola revive` relies on) landed with chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows through Run E, as measured on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/live-round.md`: `stamped 2.1.287  22 pass  0 fail`; one record round and one `run --local-live` round, six starts each), relied on every OS and not measured on Windows (owed to "Windows-only live measurements"); the `local-command-compact` row landed with chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row through Run B's `/compact` paste, as measured on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/live-round.md`: `stamped 2.1.287  24 pass  0 fail`, `compact_latency_ms` 21413; one record round, six starts), relied on every OS and not measured on Windows (owed to "Windows-only live measurements"); `send`'s use of the local-command list (`/clear`'s confirmation, `unconfirmable`) landed with chunk 2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes ([Delivery Confirmation]);
 the harness prefixes and the R8 identity floor were measured on 2.1.287 by a scratch probe at chunk 2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host (Harness prompt prefixes above; Occupied Resources → Environment variables) and landed no row: both rows stay owed, with no route entry minted for them (the founder's live answer of 2026-10-07T09:43Z, relayed by the overseer). S3/S7/S8 and dialog concurrency landed with their own re-probe (chunk 2026-10-05-dialog-rows-and-re-probe), so a non-`null` dialog decision needs a stamp whose relied rows all pass (a stamp holding exactly the fourteen older ids, or exactly the seventeen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row holds, or exactly the eighteen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-one ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-two ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board holds, or exactly the twenty-three ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row holds, all `pass`, reads unverified on every OS, and so do one holding the eighteen and `resume-session` and one holding the eighteen, `resume-session` and `agents-join` on Windows; one holding the eighteen, `resume-session`, `agents-join` and `local-command-compact` reads verified on Windows only; so every home stamped before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify`); the dated gap under which dialog answers flowed on the ten-row stamp (the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-04) is closed. The `permission` kind runs end to end since chunk 2026-10-05-permission-end-to-end (`tests/cli_answer.rs` over the gated `fixtures/fake-scripts/path4-permission.json`).
 A `question` first raised by PermissionRequest stays `null` to the human: on 2.1.288 and 2.1.287 a PermissionRequest `allow` WITH `updatedInput` would satisfy it (read statically from both installed bundles, never run), but that body has no ledger row, and adding one needs a 25th row, its `viola verify` probe and a re-stamp of every stamped version (2.1.287 and 2.1.302 today, each `24 pass  0 fail` on the Linux dev host, 2.1.302 as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows/evidence/live-round.md`; a verify is six `claude` starts). The `agents --json` join landed at chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board (row `agents-join`); plugin precedence is no row ([Plugin Scope]). The statusline pass-through landed at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through with no statusline row; its three rows landed at chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows through Run B's probe `--settings`, as measured on live 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/live-round.md`: `stamped 2.1.287  21 pass  0 fail`; one record round and one `run --local-live` round, five starts each), not measured on Windows, where they are not relied (owed to "Windows-only live measurements"). The real `claude` probe and `--record` run only locally; CI runs `verify` against the fake agent's print mode and its interactive `--screens --turn-stop --trusted-root --dialogs --framing` modes. Rationale: the docs lag the installed build, and several load-bearing behaviours are measured, not documented.

subject: dec-cli-version-compatibility
text: - Before its `cli` log opens, `viola verify` runs `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree(home, None, None)` (the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/`, each that exists); a refusal prints the home pair and exits 1 with no step line, no summary and no line. The one stamps writer, `update_stamps`, runs `strict::check_stamps` before it creates `ledger/` and again under its lock before the capped read; a refusal (`StampsError::StrictModes`, [Error Handling]) reads and writes nothing, and verify maps it to the same home pair.
